Small-error pairwise bounds for field powers

On 128 bits the fixed permutation P(x)=x7P(x)=x^7 over 𝔽2128\mathbb F_{2^{128}} brings every ordered pair within 2−1282^{-128} of uniform in at most five cipher rounds. This bound even tolerates changing up to 2622^{62} entries, provided the new table is a permutation. For the patched inverse on the same width, exactly four rounds are necessary and sufficient at this threshold. Both conclusions use fresh independent shared XOR keys and the same public permutation each round.

Public permutation Bits Type of result Rounds at 2−322^{-32} At 2−642^{-64} At 2−1282^{-128}
x7x^7, up to 2622^{62} changed entries 128 Sufficient 3 4 5
Patched inverse 128 Sufficient, last column exact 3 3 4
x7x^7 8 Exact 15 28 56
Patched inverse 8 Exact 10 19 35

The eight-bit rows illustrate why block width matters when setting an absolute error target. The computations at that width iterate exact integer counts. The large-width bounds come from the formula for PP and require no enumeration. The verifier also accepts an explicit table and checks its distance from the specified power in the supplied polynomial basis. Verifier and exact calculator

uv run --locked power_mixing.py bound --bits 128 --power 7 --security 32 64 128
uv run --locked power_mixing.py exact --modulus 0x11b --power 7 --security 32 64 128
uv run --locked power_mixing.py verify --modulus 0x11b --power 7 --file permutation.txt

A single derivative row gives the complete pair walk

Let N=2nN=2^n, m=N−1m=N-1, and let P(0)=0P(0)=0, P(x)=xdP(x)=x^d on the multiplicative group, with gcd(d,m)=1\gcd(d,m)=1. For a uniform field element UU define Z=P(U+1)+P(U)Z=P(U+1)+P(U). If a pair has difference a≠0a\ne0, its next difference has the law of adZa^d Z. This follows by writing the uniform first argument as aUaU. The fresh ZZ is independent of past differences. From start aa, after ss difference steps the result is distributed as

ads∏j=0s−1Zjdj, a^{d^s} \prod_{j=0}^{s-1} Z_j^{d^j},

with ZjZ_j independent copies. All starts have the same distance to uniform. Taking logs in the cyclic group gives an affine random walk. For its nontrivial multiplicative characters χ\chi write w(χ)=𝔼χ(Z)w(\chi)=\mathbb E\chi(Z). If TT is the difference kernel on nonzero states, then Tχ=w(χ)χdT\chi=w(\chi)\chi^d. Since the character indices are permuted by dd, the operator norm on the mean-zero subspace is exactly ρ=maxχ≠1|w(χ)|\rho=\max_{\chi\ne1}|w(\chi)|. Parseval also gives exact chi-squared distance ∑χ≠1∏j=0s−1|w(χdj)|2\sum_{\chi\ne1}\prod_{j=0}^{s-1}|w(\chi^{d^j})|^2. Thus the full cipher satisfies

d2(1+s)≤12N−2ρs.d_2(1+s)\le\tfrac12\sqrt{N-2}\,\rho^s.

Here d2(r)d_2(r) is worst-start pair TV after rr full rounds. The last uniform key randomizes the first coordinate of the pair and the last fixed permutation preserves TV. Pair-to-difference reduction · Power-function differential spectra · Affine random walks on cyclic groups

A checkable condition from low signed degree

For a positive odd exponent e>1e>1 let Fe(x)=(x+1)e+xeF_e(x)=(x+1)^e+x^e. It has degree e−1e-1 and exactly e−1e-1 simple roots over the algebraic closure. Indeed x=0,1x=0,1 are excluded, and (x+1)/x(x+1)/x gives a bijection from the roots to the nonidentity eeth roots of unity, all distinct in characteristic two. Hence for any nontrivial character of order kk this polynomial cannot be a constant multiple of a kkth power. The multiplicative Weil bound gives |w(χ)|≤(e−2)/N|w(\chi)|\le(e-2)/\sqrt N. The noise of the actual permutation has no zero values. Weil bound, Theorem 3.7

For the negative odd exponent −e-e, with zero patched to zero, use Fe(x)/(x(x+1))eF_e(x)/(x(x+1))^e away from 0,10,1, taking F1=1F_1=1. Inside a character of order kk, replace the denominator by multiplication by (x(x+1))k−(emodk)(x(x+1))^{k-(e\bmod k)}. Since ee is coprime to mm, both introduced roots have multiplicity coprime to kk. They are disjoint from the numerator roots. There are e+1e+1 distinct roots, including when e=1e=1. The character bound is eNe\sqrt N for the unnormalized sum, and restoring the two patched inputs costs at most two more. Thus ρ≤e/N+2/N\rho\le e/\sqrt N+2/N.

Multiplying the exponent by a power of two amounts to an additive Frobenius change of output coordinates. Replacing PP by its inverse transposes TT by exchanging input and output pairs in the difference counts. Both operations preserve the norm. The verifier takes the best signed degree among these equivalent representations.

If a supplied permutation differs from the certified power in at most hh table entries, its one-step difference row changes in TV by at most 2h/N2h/N. Either of the two translated inputs must hit a changed entry for a discrepancy. The inverse tables also differ in exactly hh entries, so the same inequality holds for columns. The maximal absolute row sum and column sum of the difference of the kernels are both at most 4h/N4h/N. Their geometric mean bounds the Euclidean operator norm. The new table therefore satisfies the same round guarantee with ρ+4h/N\rho+4h/N whenever this is below one. This applies to a supplied valid table even when its altered values destroy the power symmetry.

For N=2128N=2^{128}, 77 is coprime to N−1N-1, and h≤262h\le 2^{62} gives ρ+4h/N≤6/264\rho+4h/N\le6/2^{64}. Four difference steps give worst-case TV less than 2−1282^{-128}, hence five cipher rounds suffice. In compact mode the program checks the exponent condition with integer arithmetic. An externally supplied bound on hh is an assumption in this mode. The table mode verifies hh by enumeration.

Exactly four inverse rounds at error 1/N1/N

Take even n≥6n\ge6. In the patched-inverse two-step formula the probability to return to a starting difference is (2N+8)/N2(2N+8)/N^2. Its excess above 1/(N−1)1/(N-1) already exceeds 1/N1/N. Thus three cipher rounds miss the target. Three difference steps, or four cipher rounds, give

d2(4)≤1−2/N2N(1+2/N)3≤1/N,d_2(4)\le \frac{\sqrt{1-2/N}}{2N}(1+2/\sqrt N)^3\le 1/N,

since N≥64N\ge64. This proves minimality, including the 128-bit row. The inverse is a published benchmark; the calculation builds on the case analysis in the paper named in the assignment. Two-step formula · Liu, Tessaro and Vaikuntanathan, Appendix A

Exact and fallback calculations

The exact program forms one histogram in discrete-log coordinates, giving one vote per unordered pair {x,x+1}\{x,x+1\}. To advance a row it permutes its indices by dd and cyclically convolves with the histogram. After ss steps the common denominator is (N/2)s(N/2)^s. With integer counts cjc_j and denominator DD, the test for TV ≤2−k\le2^{-k} is 2k∑j|mcj−D|≤2mD2^k\sum_j|m c_j-D|\le2mD. Packing the coefficients into nonoverlapping base-256256 digit groups reduces each cyclic convolution to one integer multiplication and a wraparound addition. Only O(N)O(N) counts are stored. Their bit length grows with the number of rounds.

The support of ZZ contains 11. Its discrete logs generate the entire cyclic group precisely when their gcd with mm is one. Otherwise the walk from 11 stays in a proper subgroup. When the gcd is one, every nontrivial character sees at least two different phases and hence has |w(χ)|<1|w(\chi)|<1. This decides convergence without a dense matrix. For nonlinear permutation powers the full-group case also follows from Lenstra’s character-preserver theorem: if a quotient by a proper noise subgroup existed, PP would induce exponentiation by dd on the quotient of every nonzero difference, forcing a semilinear affine map. Here P(0)=0,P(1)=1P(0)=0,P(1)=1, so it would be Frobenius. Stafford’s group theorem gives an independent route covering higher orders. Lenstra, Theorem 3 · Stafford, 1998

This yields a coarse guarantee even if the Weil estimate exceeds one. Two distinct phases each have mass at least 2/N2/N. Removing this mass from each and applying the triangle inequality gives |w(χ)|≤1−(4/N)(1−cos(π/m))≤1−8/(Nm2)|w(\chi)|\le1-(4/N)(1-\cos(\pi/m))\le1-8/(Nm^2). The last step uses sinv≥2v/π\sin v\ge2v/\pi on [0,π/2][0,\pi/2]. The compact calculator uses this fallback for unmodified nonlinear powers. For Frobenius powers, every derivative is deterministic and pairs fail to mix for n≥2n\ge2.

Attribution. The homogeneity of power derivatives, Fourier analysis of affine cyclic walks, character estimates, and the semilinear/group classifications are published. The pairwise formulas and round certificates here are applications of those results to one repeated public permutation. The exact finite measurements are project computations. Publication priority for the quantitative specialization and perturbation guarantee remains unverified.
